implementation_notes: Ktor plugins sit between the call and the routing handler, so the detour is a plugin installed only when the configuration says so: install(AuditPlugin) adds interception phases (onCall, onCallRespond) globally or - inside a route block - for one subtree only, while the same routing handler remains the destination. Without a server framework the toggle in a Kotlin flow is a conditional operator splice (val route = if (cfg.detourEnabled) flow.onEach { audit(it) } else flow), which leaves the terminal collector unchanged. Note that Ktor installs plugins once at application start, so a live switch belongs inside the plugin as a per-call predicate.
pitfalls: An if around install() only toggles at start-up; for a runtime switch keep the plugin installed and test the flag per call.
Re-installing the same plugin on a route merges configurations and the last installation wins - a route-scoped reinstall can silently replace the global one.
Ktor 2 and Ktor 3 differ in the plugin API (Plugin vs createApplicationPlugin/BaseApplicationPlugin); pin the version before copying snippets.
